title: Dynamic models of segregation†
abstract: Some segregation results from the practices of organizations, some from specialized communication systems, some from correlation with a variable that is non-random; and some results from the interplay of individual choices. This is an abstract study of the interactive dynamics of discriminatory individual choices. One model is a simulation in which individual members of two recognizable groups distribute themselves in neighborhoods defined by reference to their own locations. A second model is analytic and deals with compartmented space. A final section applies the analytics to ‘neighborhood tipping.’ The systemic effects are found to be overwhelming: there is no simple correspondence of individual incentive to collective results. Exaggerated separation and patterning result from the dynamics of movement. Inferences about individual motives can usually not be drawn from aggregate patterns. Some unexpected phenomena, like density and vacancy, are generated. A general theory of ‘tipping’ begins to emerge. © 1971, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.
abstractZh: 有些隔离源于组织的做法，有些源于专门化的沟通系统，有些源于与非随机变量的相关性，还有些源于个体选择之间的相互作用。本文对具有区别对待倾向的个体选择的交互动态进行抽象研究。第一个模型采用模拟方法，让两个可辨识群体的个体成员分布在以自身位置为参照定义的邻里中。第二个模型采用解析方法，处理被分隔的空间。最后一部分将解析方法用于“邻里倾覆”。研究发现，系统效应具有决定性作用：个体激励与集体结果之间不存在简单对应关系。移动动态会产生被放大的分离与空间模式，通常无法从聚合模式推断个体动机。模型还产生了密度、空置等一些意外现象，并初步形成一般性的“倾覆”理论。
